computation.problem_statement: The leaf carries no number: an empty ledger asserts 'this rotation entry has no dependency to resolve'. Two things are therefore checkable from cached wiki text: (a) the cardinality — does Aatrox's priced rotation have exactly seven entries? and (b) the content — is each entry's damage a self-contained function of its own cached leveling row plus attacker/target stats, with no input taken from another entry's output?

step_a_cardinality.claim: Seven is the correct number of rotation entries for Aatrox.
step_a_cardinality.derivation: data/champion-audit/batch-e9-1.json, Aatrox, verdict 'ok', enumerates exactly the modeled families: 'R World Ender modeled as %total-AD stat buff; Q 3-cast, W two-hit, P %maxHP on-hit all sourced from the JSON', with slots P=modeled, Q=modeled, W=modeled, E=out_of_scope, R=modeled. Counting priced rows: Q 3-cast = 3, W two-hit = 2, P empowered auto = 1, R stat buff = 1, E excluded (heal passive only, no enemy-damage row) => 3+2+1+1 = 7.

(data/champions.json Aatrox Q effect 0) — and the cache carries three separate leveling rows, First / Second / Third Cast Damage, so each cast is its own priced row.

step_b_content.claim: Every one of the seven ledgers is correctly EMPTY.
step_b_content.derivation: A dependency ledger is non-empty only if an entry's value must be resolved from another entry's output. In step 0 I priced Aatrox's whole rotation to the corpus's 0.1-precision numbers using, for each row, only (i) that row's own cached leveling row and (ii) attacker/target stat totals. No row consumed another row's output: Q reads the cached 3-cast sweetspot total, W reads the cached two-hit total, P reads the target's max health, R writes the attacker's own AD before rows are priced. There is nothing for a resolver to record, so an empty ledger on each of the seven is the correct content, and the old <absent> merely omitted the field rather than asserting a different value.
step_b_content.boundary_noted_honestly: Aatrox's kit does contain sequencing preconditions (Q2 requires Q1 within the 4s recast window; W's second hit requires the tether to survive 1.5s; P's cooldown is cut 2s per ability/auto hit, 4s on a Sweetspot). If 'dependencies' were a kit-prerequisite graph rather than a value-resolution ledger, those ledgers would be non-empty. It is a value-resolution ledger under a resolver, and the numeric evidence above shows no value in the priced rotation is resolved from another entry — so empty is right. Likewise R's +40% total AD is applied as a stat-phase buff (it is already inside the 203.0 AD that reproduces 863.7 and 157.5), not as a rotation-entry input, so it does not populate Q's or W's ledger.
